text:
alex_k: heads up — during the KEK migration for envelope encryption in staging we hit an auth gap. moved keys from tenant-A kv -> central tenant-B kv, assigned a managed identity to the new KV but a couple services got 403 on wrapKey.
rita_s: did you switch from Access Policies to RBAC on the vault? that usually flips which principal types can do crypto ops.
alex_k: yes we toggled to RBAC to standardize. our CI runner uses a service principal from tenant-A. MI was created in tenant-B cluster; looks like cross-tenant principal can't be granted RBAC on the vault.
samir_r: cross-tenant access is hairy. RBAC uses AAD object ids scoped to the vault's tenant — you can't assign a principal from another tenant unless it's a guest/service principal in the vault tenant.
alex_k: we tried adding the SP as a guest in tenant-B and then role-assigned Key Vault Crypto User, but wrapKey still failed with "Principal not found" for some hosts.
jess_m: double-check the assignment propagation — az role assignment create can take a few seconds, and AAD replication can be minutes. Also confirm the principal type (servicePrincipal vs user) in the role assignment record.
infra-bot: deploy log: "2026-02-12T16:22:41Z - assign-role --assignee 7f3... --role 'Key Vault Crypto Service' --scope /subscriptions/..../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/central-kv" (ok)
rita_s: also check vault firewall & private endpoint. if the vault only allows selected networks, the wrapping call could be blocked from some hosts even if auth is ok.
alex_k: good catch — staging VMs are on an approved subnet but our CI runner container uses ephemeral IP through NAT gateway that wasn't in the allowlist.
samir_r: other thing: if you maintain access policies AND RBAC, conflict can occur — Access Policies are legacy and if they're present you have to be careful about permission precedence.
alex_k: wait — we had access policies disabled earlier. so it's RBAC-only. question: for rotation how do people handle rewrapping DEKs without downtime? we're considering double-wrap approach.
security_oncall: recommended pattern: 1) create new KEK; 2) provision and test background rewrap job that reads DEK, calls wrapKey(newKEK, DEK), writes new envelope record but keep old envelope; 3) switch readers to prefer new envelope id but fallback to old; 4) after a retention window delete/rotate old KEK. make sure operations are idempotent and job is resumable.
rita_s: and enable KV diagnostic logs to a storage account/Log Analytics so you can audit wrap/unwrap ops per principal: enable 'AuditEvent' and 'CryptographicOperations' categories in diagnostic settings.
alex_k: any gotchas for rotation across tenants? like re-encrypting DEKs that were originally wrapped by tenant-A key with tenant-B key.
samir_r: rewrap itself is independent — you unwrap with the original KEK (requires access) to get DEK plaintext, then wrap with new KEK. main issue is ensuring you still have access to original KEK during migration window. consider doing a staged rewrap where you minimize the time the plaintext is in memory and use HSM-backed ops when possible.
jess_m: if you can't get access to original tenant keys (e.g., decommissioned SP), you might need to request cross-tenant key export — often not allowed. so plan retention and rotation windows ahead.
security_oncall: operational notes: enable soft-delete and purge protection on the vault to avoid accidental deletion during migration. set alerts on failed wrap/unwrap rates and increase log retention for at least 90 days during migration.
rita_s: for auditing, link KV diagnostics to Sentinel/Log Analytics. create analytic rule for anomalous wrapKey volume from a single principal (could indicate exfil attempts).
alex_k: quick verification commands we used:
```
az keyvault set-policy --name central-kv --object-id <guest-sp-object-id> --key-permissions wrapKey unwrapKey
az role assignment create --assignee <guest-sp-id> --role "Key Vault Crypto User" --scope /subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/central-kv
```
these looked OK but calls still failed from CI (403).
samir_r: try the REST call with the SP token from the CI host and examine WWW-Authenticate header and token audience. sometimes MSAL issues tokens with wrong resource (should be https://vault.azure.net).
jess_m: also check managed identity token if used — resource/audience must be `https://vault.azure.net` not `https://management.azure.com/`.
alex_k: thanks — token audience was wrong on a kube-service-account sidecar. fixed that and wrapKey started succeeding from most runners.
security_oncall: followups/actions:
- alex_k: run full rewrap dry-run against 10% of DEKs and post job logs here (due EOD)
- rita_s: verify diagnostic settings/alerts on central-kv and add workbook (due tomorrow)
- samir_r: document cross-tenant onboarding checklist for vault RBAC vs access policies (add to repo infra/security)
- jess_m: ensure CI token audience is enforced in auth helper library
alex_k: noted, starting dry-run now. will post summary soon. :thumbsup:
